::: {#sol-rnn-shape}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
recurrent = nn.RNN(8, 32, batch_first=True)
rows = x_train[:16].reshape(16, 8, 8)
states, last_state = recurrent(rows)
same_last = torch.equal(states[:, -1], last_state[0])
print(rows.shape, states.shape, last_state.shape, same_last)
```

With `batch_first=True`,
the input has [shape](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-shape) $16 \times 8 \times 8$:
16 sequences of 8 steps,
each step a row of 8 pixels.
The first output holds the [hidden state](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-hidden-state) after every step,
with shape $16 \times 8 \times 32$.
The second holds the hidden state after the last step only,
with shape $1 \times 16 \times 32$.
Its first dimension counts stacked layers times directions,
here 1 layer read in 1 direction [@pytorch_rnn].
Its entries `r if (py$same_last) "equal" else "differ from"` the last step of the first output.
Without `batch_first=True`,
PyTorch expects the steps first and the sequences second.

:::
